org.portico.bindings.jgroups.wan.local

Class Gateway

  • java.lang.Object
    • org.portico.bindings.jgroups.wan.local.Gateway

  • public class Gateway
extends Object
    This class is the gateway to the wider WAN network for the local connection. Messages sent here are forwarded to other connections via the WAN router. ### Lifecycle All connections will create an instance of this class, but the internal mechanics will not be started unless WAN mode is enabled in the RID file. This class starts _TWO DISTINCT THREADS_. The first reads incoming messages from the socket that connects us to the WAN router. The other is started by the Bundler and sends outgoing messages to the router. ### Sending to the WAN As the JGroups `ChannelListener` receives messages from the local cluster, they both given to the local federate for processing, but also forwarded here to be sent to the gateway. The method forwardToGateway(ControlHeader, Message) does that processing, handing messages off to the Bundler, which will send them over the WAN in an efficient manner. ### Receiving messages from the WAN Messages are received from the WAN by the `GatewayListener` inner class which is running its own separate thread. When received, they are packaged into JGroups `Message` types and handed off to the Channel class to be sent to the local cluster. Note that messages are *NOT* immediately processed locally. The Portico JGroups configuration loops all messages back to the local member, so rather than explicitly process them as received, we catch them as they're looped back just as if they came from the local cluster.
